"""Click analytics: one row per successful redirect, none for failures."""
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

from conftest import TS_FORMAT, assert_error_envelope, parse_ts


def test_a_successful_redirect_increments_the_click_count_exactly_once(app):
    code = app.create("https://example.com/a").json()["code"]

    assert app.stats(code).json()["total_clicks"] == 0
    assert app.visit(code).status_code == 307

    assert len(app.click_rows()) == 1, "exactly one click row per redirect"
    assert app.stats(code).json()["total_clicks"] == 1


def test_three_redirects_produce_three_clicks_and_a_total_of_three(app):
    code = app.create("https://example.com/a").json()["code"]

    for _ in range(3):
        assert app.visit(code).status_code == 307

    assert len(app.click_rows()) == 3
    assert app.stats(code).json()["total_clicks"] == 3

    assert app.visit("Qq1Ww2E").status_code == 404

    assert len(app.click_rows()) == 1
    assert app.stats(code).json()["total_clicks"] == 1

    app.set_expiry(code, datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=5))

    assert len(app.click_rows()) == 1, "clicks were recorded for a refused redirect"
    assert app.stats(code).json()["total_clicks"] == 1

"""Short code collisions are retried instead of blowing up or hanging."""
import re

from conftest import assert_error_envelope

CODE_RE = re.compile("^[A-Za-z0-9]{7}$")


def test_a_generator_that_repeats_an_existing_code_is_retried_until_it_is_unique(app, force_codes):
    first = app.create("https://example.com/first")
    assert first.status_code == 201, first.text
    taken = first.json()["code"]

    stub = force_codes(app, [taken, taken, "Zq7Xk2M"])
    second = app.create("https://example.com/second")

    assert stub.calls >= 2, (
        "the code generator was consulted {0} time(s): either the service did not "
        "retry after the UNIQUE collision, or the generator could not be "
        "intercepted by the test".format(stub.calls)
    )
    assert second.status_code == 201, (
        "a collision must be retried, not surfaced as {0}: {1}".format(
            second.status_code, second.text[:200]
        )
    )
    code = second.json()["code"]
    assert code != taken, "the second link reused the first link's code"
    assert CODE_RE.match(code), code

    stored = [row["code"] for row in app.link_rows()]
    assert sorted(stored) == sorted([taken, code])
    assert len(set(stored)) == 2


def test_the_retried_link_still_redirects_to_its_own_destination(app, force_codes):
    first = app.create("https://example.com/first")
    taken = first.json()["code"]
    force_codes(app, [taken, "Zq7Xk2M"])

    second = app.create("https://example.com/second")
    assert second.status_code == 201, second.text
    code = second.json()["code"]

    assert app.visit(taken).headers["location"] == "https://example.com/first"
    assert app.visit(code).headers["location"] == "https://example.com/second"


def test_exhausting_links_code_max_attempts_fails_with_503_not_500(app_factory, force_codes):
    app = app_factory(LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS="3")
    taken = app.create("https://example.com/first").json()["code"]

    stub = force_codes(app, [taken] * 50)
    response = app.create("https://example.com/second")

    assert stub.calls >= 2, (
        "generator consulted {0} time(s); the bounded retry loop never ran".format(stub.calls)
    )
    assert response.status_code == 503, (
        "a permanently colliding generator must give up with 503, got {0}: {1}".format(
            response.status_code, response.text[:200]

"""Expiry: default TTL, explicit instants, rejection of the past, and 410.

Time is controlled by writing the expires_at column, never by sleeping.
"""
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import pytest

from conftest import assert_error_envelope, parse_ts


def test_omitting_expires_at_stores_created_at_plus_the_configured_ttl_days(app):
    body = app.create("https://example.com/a").json()

    created = parse_ts(body["created_at"])
    expires = parse_ts(body["expires_at"])
    delta = abs((expires - created) - timedelta(days=30))
    assert delta <= timedelta(seconds=1), (
        "default TTL must be LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_DAYS=30 days, got "
        + str(expires - created)
    )
    row = app.link_rows()[0]
    assert parse_ts(row["expires_at"]) == expires


def test_configured_ttl_days_is_honoured_instead_of_a_hard_coded_thirty(app_factory):
    app = app_factory(LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_DAYS="3")

    body = app.create("https://example.com/a").json()

    delta = parse_ts(body["expires_at"]) - parse_ts(body["created_at"])
    assert abs(delta - timedelta(days=3)) <= timedelta(seconds=1), delta


def test_explicit_future_expires_at_is_stored_and_returned_normalized_to_utc(app):
    response = app.create("https://example.com/a", expires_at="2999-01-01T12:00:00+02:00")

    assert response.status_code == 201, response.text
    expected = datetime(2999, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    assert parse_ts(response.json()["expires_at"]) == expected
    assert parse_ts(app.link_rows()[0]["expires_at"]) == expected

"""Health endpoint and the promise that no destination is ever fetched."""

import pytest


def test_health_reports_ok_when_the_database_answers(app):

def test_neither_creation_nor_redirect_opens_an_outbound_connection(app, monkeypatch):
    attempts = []

    def refuse(*args, **kwargs):
        attempts.append(args)
        raise AssertionError("the service tried to contact the destination")

    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "connect", refuse)
    monkeypatch.setattr(socket.socket, "connect_ex", refuse)
    monkeypatch.setattr(socket, "create_connection", refuse)
    try:
        import httpx

        async def refuse_async(*args, **kwargs):
            attempts.append(args)
            raise AssertionError("the service built an HTTP client for the destination")

        monkeypatch.setattr(httpx.AsyncClient, "send", refuse_async, raising=False)
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
        pass
    try:
        import urllib.request

        monkeypatch.setattr(urllib.request, "urlopen", refuse)
    except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
        pass

    created = app.create("https://example.com/page?a=1")
    assert created.status_code == 201, created.text[:200]
    code = created.json()["code"]

    redirected = app.visit(code)
    assert redirected.status_code == 307
    assert redirected.headers["location"] == "https://example.com/page?a=1"
    assert attempts == [], "an outbound connection was attempted"

"""Creation rate limiting is per client key, returns 429, and persists no IP."""
from conftest import assert_error_envelope

CALLER = {"X-Forwarded-For": "203.0.113.10"}
OTHER = {"X-Forwarded-For": "198.51.100.7"}


def _limited_app(app_factory, **extra):
    return app_factory(
        LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR="true", **extra
    )


def test_creation_beyond_the_configured_limit_returns_429_with_retry_after_and_writes_no_row(app_factory):
    app = _limited_app(app_factory)

    for i in range(10):
        response = app.create("https://example.com/{0}".format(i), headers=CALLER)
        assert response.status_code == 201, (i, response.status_code, response.text[:200])

    blocked = app.create("https://example.com/eleven", headers=CALLER)

    assert blocked.status_code == 429, (
        "the 11th creation in the window must be refused, got {0}".format(blocked.status_code)
    )
    assert_error_envelope(blocked)
    retry_after = blocked.headers.get("retry-after")
    assert retry_after is not None, "a 429 must carry Retry-After"
    assert int(retry_after) >= 1, retry_after
    assert len(app.link_rows()) == 10, "the throttled request must not have written a row"


def test_the_limit_is_per_client_key_so_another_address_still_gets_201(app_factory):
    app = _limited_app(app_factory)
    for i in range(10):
        assert app.create("https://example.com/{0}".format(i), headers=CALLER).status_code == 201
    assert app.create("https://example.com/over", headers=CALLER).status_code == 429

    other = app.create("https://example.com/other-client", headers=OTHER)

    assert other.status_code == 201, (
        "a different client address must not be locked out by the first one's burst: "
        + other.text[:200]
    )
    assert len(app.link_rows()) == 11


def test_links_rate_limit_max_is_read_from_the_environment_rather_than_hard_coded(app_factory):
    app = _limited_app(app_factory, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX="2")

    first = app.create("https://example.com/1", headers=CALLER)
    second = app.create("https://example.com/2", headers=CALLER)
    third = app.create("https://example.com/3", headers=CALLER)

    assert (first.status_code, second.status_code) == (201, 201)
    assert third.status_code == 429, third.text[:200]
    assert len(app.link_rows()) == 2


def test_the_limiter_can_be_disabled_with_links_rate_limit_enabled_false(app_factory):
    app = app_factory(LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="false", LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR="true")

    for i in range(15):
        response = app.create("https://example.com/{0}".format(i), headers=CALLER)
        assert response.status_code == 201, (i, response.text[:200])

    assert len(app.link_rows()) == 15


def test_exercising_the_limiter_writes_no_client_address_to_disk(app_factory):
    app = _limited_app(app_factory)
    address = "203.0.113.77"
    for i in range(12):
        app.create("https://example.com/{0}".format(i), headers={"X-Forwarded-For": address})

    blob = app.disk_bytes()

    assert address.encode() not in blob, "a client IP reached persistent storage"
    for table in ("links", "clicks"):
        for column in app.columns(table):
            low = column.lower()
            assert "ip" not in low and "addr" not in low and "remote" not in low, (
                "{0}.{1} looks like it can hold a client address".format(table, column)
            )

parsed.overview: A single-node FastAPI URL shortener with three existing routes (create, redirect, stats) backed by SQLite in WAL mode. This change is additive and confined to the ASGI rate-limiting middleware and the frozen Settings snapshot: when SHORTENER_API_KEYS is configured and the request presents an exactly-matching X-API-Key on POST /api/links, the request is charged against that key's own per-minute bucket instead of the shared per-IP creation bucket. No route, schema, response body or existing environment variable changes; the only new observable behaviour is an additional 429 condition on POST /api/links.

configuration.name: LINKS_DB_PATH
configuration.purpose: Filesystem path to the SQLite database file. Tests that assert persistence must set this exact name; there is no DATABASE_PATH.

configuration.name: LINKS_BASE_URL
configuration.purpose: Origin used to build the short_url field in POST /api/links responses. Trailing slash is stripped at parse time.

configuration.name: LINKS_CODE_LENGTH
configuration.purpose: Number of base62 characters in a generated short code. Clamped to [4,16]; unparsable values degrade to 7 with a warning.

configuration.name: LINKS_CODE_MAX_RETRIES
configuration.purpose: Total insert attempts allowed when a generated code collides with the UNIQUE constraint before returning 503.

configuration.name: LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH
configuration.purpose: Maximum accepted length of the target url field on POST /api/links.

configuration.name: LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: Default link lifetime in seconds when the request omits expires_in. Empty string means links never expire (expires_at NULL).

configuration.name: LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: Upper bound accepted for the expires_in request field.

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
configuration.purpose: Master switch for the ASGI rate-limit middleware. When false, neither the per-IP buckets nor the API-key buckets are consulted and no 429 is ever produced.

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX
configuration.purpose: Requests per window allowed in the per-IP 'create' bucket. The 'redirect' bucket allows LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER (module constant 100).

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: Fixed window length in seconds, shared by the per-IP buckets and every API-key bucket. Also the ceiling for the Retry-After value.

configuration.name: LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS
configuration.purpose: Maximum number of live buckets retained per bucket namespace ('create', 'redirect', 'create_key'). Each namespace prunes independently, so adding key buckets cannot shrink the per-IP capacity.

configuration.name: LINKS_LOG_LEVEL
configuration.purpose: Root logger level for the application. At DEBUG the limiter logs bucket namespace and salted-hash prefix only, never the raw API key or client address.

configuration.name: SHORTENER_API_KEYS
configuration.purpose: Comma-separated name:quota pairs, e.g. "alpha:100,beta:20", giving each recognised X-API-Key value its own per-window creation quota. Names and quotas are whitespace-trimmed. Entries with no colon, an empty name, or a quota that is not an integer >= 1 are skipped with a warning. Unset or empty means no keys are configured and behaviour is identical to before this change. Read once into the frozen Settings snapshot at app construction.

endpoints.summary: Create a short link. This is the only route whose limiting can be charged to an API key.
endpoints.request: Headers: Content-Type: application/json (required); X-API-Key: optional opaque string, matched case-insensitively as a header name but its VALUE is compared byte-exactly and case-sensitively against the parsed SHORTENER_API_KEYS names. Body: {"url": string, required, 1..LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH chars, must parse as an absolute http:// or https:// URL with a non-empty host; "expires_in": optional integer seconds, 1..LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS, null or omitted means LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS (which itself may mean no expiry)}. Unknown body fields are ignored. Presenting an unrecognised key value is never an authentication failure: it is treated as if no key were presented.
endpoints.response: 201 body {"code": string (base62, LINKS_CODE_LENGTH chars), "short_url": string (LINKS_BASE_URL + "/" + code), "target_url": string, "created_at": string (RFC 3339 UTC, e.g. 2024-05-01T12:00:00Z), "expires_at": string RFC 3339 UTC or null}. Errors always {"error":{"code": string, "message": string}} with codes: invalid_json (400), validation_error (422), rate_limited (429), code_generation_failed (503), internal_error (500). A 429 carries Retry-After (decimal whole seconds, >=1 and <=LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, no fractional part) and Cache-Control: no-store, and its body never contains or reflects the presented X-API-Key value.

status_codes.when: URL validated, a unique code inserted into links.
Request body is not well-formed JSON or is not a JSON object.
url missing, empty, longer than LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH, not an absolute http/https URL, or expires_in out of range / not an integer.

Rate limiting is enabled AND either (a) X-API-Key matched a configured key exactly and that key's bucket has already served its quota in the current window, or (b) no key was presented or the presented value is unrecognised and the per-IP 'create' bucket has served LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX in the current window. Rejected in ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so no row is written to links.
LINKS_CODE_MAX_RETRIES insert attempts all hit the UNIQUE constraint on links.code.
Unhandled database or serialisation error.

endpoints.summary: Resolve a short code and redirect. Never limited by API key.
endpoints.request: Path param code: 1..16 chars matching ^[0-9A-Za-z]+$; anything else is treated as not found. X-API-Key, if present, is ignored entirely on this route (neither authenticating nor rebucketing). Routes under /api are matched first and never reach this handler.
endpoints.response: 307 with Location: stored target_url, Cache-Control: no-store and an empty body. Errors use {"error":{"code":"not_found"|"rate_limited","message":...}}.

status_codes.when: Code exists and (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now).
Code does not exist, has expired, or does not match the code character class. The body is byte-identical in all three cases.
Rate limiting is enabled and the per-IP 'redirect' bucket has served LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 requests in the current window. Unaffected by any API key state, including an exhausted key quota.

endpoints.summary: Return click analytics for a code. Never rate limited.
endpoints.request: Path param code as above. X-API-Key, if present, is ignored and does not affect the outcome.
endpoints.response: 200 body {"code": string, "target_url": string, "created_at": RFC 3339 UTC string, "expires_at": RFC 3339 UTC string or null, "expired": boolean, "click_count": integer >= 0, "last_clicked_at": RFC 3339 UTC string or null}. Error body {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":...}}.

No row in links for that code, or the code fails the character class.

decisions.decision: Request for an expired code
decisions.choice: 404 with body {"error":{"code":"not_found",...}}, byte-identical to a code that never existed. Expired rows are filtered by the SELECT predicate, not deleted on the read path.
decisions.rationale: A caller cannot tell whether a short code was ever issued, so an expired-link probe cannot be used to enumerate the link table; the human-visible result is the same dead-link page either way.
rejected: 410 Gone: distinguishes expired from never-issued, confirming to a scanner that a code was real and is worth retrying later.
Deleting the row on read: destroys the stats history that GET /api/links/{code}/stats must still serve with expired:true.

decisions.decision: Where the click analytics write happens relative to the redirect response
decisions.choice: A single INSERT INTO clicks executed synchronously inside the redirect handler, committed before the 307 response is returned. No BackgroundTask, no queue.
decisions.rationale: Stats are correct the instant after a redirect, which is what both the tests and an operator checking a link they just clicked expect; in WAL mode on a single node the insert is sub-millisecond and does not block readers.
rejected: Starlette BackgroundTask after the response: clicks recorded after a client disconnect or during shutdown are silently dropped and stats become non-deterministic in tests.
In-memory batch flushed periodically: loses the tail of the buffer on every restart and would need new state that must not be persisted.

decisions.decision: Layer at which rate limiting is enforced and what it is keyed by
decisions.choice: Pure ASGI middleware installed ahead of routing and body parsing. It inspects scope['path'], scope['method'] and scope['headers'] only. Keying: POST /api/links -> salted hash of the exact X-API-Key value in namespace 'create_key' if it is a configured key, else salted hash of scope['client'][0] in namespace 'create'; GET /{code} (any path not under /api) -> salted hash of the client address in namespace 'redirect' at quota LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100; /api/links/{code}/stats -> not limited at all.
decisions.rationale: A throttled creation is rejected before a database connection is acquired or a body is read, so flooding costs the service one dict lookup; and an exhausted creation quota provably cannot break redirects, which are the user-visible product.
rejected: FastAPI dependency on the route: the body is already parsed and validated by then, so a flood still costs pydantic work and the middleware ordering guarantee in the constraints is lost.
Keying on X-Forwarded-For: unset by this deployment's contract and trivially spoofable, which would let one client mint unlimited identities.
Reverse-proxy-level limiting: cannot see X-API-Key semantics or per-key quotas, and would need a config surface outside this repo.

decisions.decision: How API key values are kept out of storage and logs
decisions.choice: The raw key never leaves the request scope. It is hashed with blake2b under a per-boot random salt to form the bucket identity; only the namespace and the first 8 hex chars of that hash are ever logged, and only at DEBUG. Settings.api_key_quotas is excluded from repr and from startup config logging. No 429 body or header echoes the presented value.
decisions.rationale: Grepping the database directory, the WAL, or DEBUG logs for the literal key value or a client IP finds nothing, so a leaked disk image or log bundle does not leak credentials.
rejected: Storing a static hash of the key: a static digest is a stable pseudonym that survives restarts and can be rainbow-tabled against a guessable key list.
Logging the key at DEBUG for support: the criteria forbid it and DEBUG logs routinely leave the trust boundary.

decisions.decision: Window algorithm and Retry-After computation
decisions.choice: Fixed window of LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS anchored at the first request in that window, shared by all namespaces. Retry-After = max(1, min(window, ceil(window_start + window - clock()))) rendered as a decimal integer string, with Cache-Control: no-store on every 429.
decisions.rationale: A client that honours Retry-After waits a whole number of seconds between 1 and 60 and is then admitted, and the header never contains a fractional value that some clients reject outright.
rejected: Sliding-window log: unbounded memory per identity and changes the existing per-IP behaviour the constraints freeze.
Token bucket: allows a burst past the exact Nth-request boundary the criteria assert on.

decisions.decision: Failure mode for malformed SHORTENER_API_KEYS
decisions.choice: Parse entry-by-entry at construction. Trim whitespace around names and quotas. Skip any entry lacking a colon, with an empty name, or with a quota that is not an integer >= 1; log one WARNING naming the ordinal position and the reason but never the raw text. Keep every usable entry. A totally unusable value degrades to an empty mapping.
decisions.rationale: "alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20" starts the app with delta limited at 20 while alpha, beta and gamma quietly fall back to the per-IP limit, instead of a crash loop that takes the whole shortener down over one typo.
rejected: Raising at import or startup: one bad character in an env var becomes a total outage.
Discarding the entire mapping when any entry is bad: the delta:20 criterion fails and operators lose working keys to an unrelated typo.

decisions.decision: Storage engine and connection mode (unchanged, restated for the contract)
decisions.choice: SQLite at LINKS_DB_PATH in WAL mode with a per-request connection, foreign_keys ON, busy_timeout 5000ms.
decisions.rationale: Deployment is single node and the redirect path is a primary-key lookup, so WAL lets the synchronous click INSERT proceed without blocking concurrent redirect reads.
rejected: Postgres: a second process to operate for a workload whose hot query is one index seek.
Rollback-journal mode: the click INSERT would take an exclusive lock and stall concurrent redirects.

decisions.decision: Interaction with LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false
decisions.choice: When disabled, the middleware short-circuits before any bucket lookup, including key buckets, so a key with quota 1 still permits unlimited creations.
decisions.rationale: The single documented off switch really turns everything off; an operator debugging a load test does not have to also unset SHORTENER_API_KEYS.
rejected: Treating configured keys as an always-on limiter: 15 creations with alpha:1 would fail, contradicting the criteria and surprising anyone who set the flag to false.

redirect_status_code.rationale: 307 preserves the request method and body, so a POST or HEAD against a short code arrives at the target unchanged rather than being silently rewritten to GET as 302 permits. Combined with Cache-Control: no-store it is non-cacheable, which is what makes revocation real: every click comes back to the service, so deleting or expiring a malicious link takes effect on the very next click and every click is counted in the clicks table. A 301 (or any permanently cacheable redirect) would be retained by browsers and intermediaries effectively forever — after a link is found to be malicious the client stops asking us and keeps sending users to the target, and those clicks never appear in click_count, so both the kill switch and the analytics silently stop working. 302 was rejected only because of the method-rewriting licence; its caching properties are otherwise acceptable.

short_code_strategy.generation: secrets.choice over the 62-character alphabet, once per character, drawing from the OS CSPRNG (os.urandom). 7 characters is ~41.7 bits of entropy, about 3.5e12 codes: an attacker guessing at 1000 requests/second (well above the redirect bucket's LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per minute) needs on the order of a century to find one live link, while the code stays short enough to read aloud. Sequential or counter-derived codes are rejected outright: an incrementing id lets anyone walk from 1 upward and read every URL every user ever shortened. Hashing the target URL is also rejected: it leaks whether a given URL was already shortened, forces two unrelated users to share one code and one click count, and makes revocation for one user break the link for the other.
short_code_strategy.uniqueness: Enforced solely by the PRIMARY KEY (UNIQUE) constraint on links.code inside SQLite. The handler does not SELECT to check availability first; it inserts and lets the database arbitrate, so two concurrent inserts of the same code cannot both succeed.
short_code_strategy.collision_handling: The insert is attempted at most LINKS_CODE_MAX_RETRIES (default 5) times, generating a fresh random code each attempt and catching sqlite3.IntegrityError on the code constraint only (any other IntegrityError propagates as 500). There is no unbounded loop. When all attempts are exhausted the request returns 503 with {"error":{"code":"code_generation_failed","message":"Could not allocate a unique short code, please retry."}} and an ERROR log recording the attempt count, which is the signal to raise LINKS_CODE_LENGTH.

open_questions: Whether per-key quotas should also apply to GET /api/links/{code}/stats. Safe default as specified: stats is never rate limited by any bucket.

Whether a keyed 429 should include X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset headers. Safe default: it must not, because Limit would disclose the key's configured quota; only Retry-After and Cache-Control: no-store are emitted.
Whether unrecognised keys should eventually be rejected with 401 behind an opt-in flag. Safe default: no such flag exists in this release; unknown keys fall back to the per-IP bucket.

Pruning policy detail for the 'create_key' namespace when LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS is reached. Safe default: evict the entries whose windows expired longest ago first, and if none have expired, refuse to add a new bucket and fall back to the per-IP bucket for that request rather than evicting a live one.
Whether Retry-After should also be emitted on the per-IP redirect 429. Safe default: keep today's behaviour byte-for-byte, whatever it is, since the redirect path is explicitly frozen.

Time source for expires_at comparison versus the limiter clock. Safe default: expiry uses wall-clock UTC (datetime.now(timezone.utc)); the limiter uses the injectable monotonic clock at app.state.rate_limiter.clock, and the two are never mixed.

payload.system:
You are the API designer for an automated software delivery pipeline. Your output is the contract that implementation, tests and documentation are each generated from independently. Anything you leave vague gets decided three times, differently, and the tests will agree with the code while both disagree with the docs.

Design the smallest API that satisfies the acceptance criteria. Every endpoint you add is code, tests, docs and attack surface that someone maintains.

For each endpoint give the method, the path, the request shape with its validation rules, the response shape, and every status code it can return including the failures. An endpoint listed with only its happy path is not designed yet.

The data model states columns with types, nullability, uniqueness and the indexes the read path depends on. If a query on the hot path would scan the table, say so and add the index.

Decisions carry rationale and the alternative you rejected. "Use SQLite" is not a decision. "SQLite in WAL mode, because deployment is single node and the redirect path is a primary key lookup" is.

Two decisions are mandatory for a redirect service.

Redirect status code. Choose 302 or 307 and justify it in terms of what the service loses otherwise. A 301 is cached by browsers and intermediaries effectively forever: after a link is found to be malicious it cannot be killed because the client stops asking the service, and every one of those clicks is invisible to analytics. Pick 307 when the request method must survive the redirect, 302 otherwise. Put the choice and the reasoning in redirect_status_code, and do not leave it to the implementer.

Short code generation. Codes are drawn at random from a base62 alphabet, uniqueness is enforced by a UNIQUE constraint in the database rather than by a check before the insert, and a collision retries a small bounded number of times before returning a clean error instead of looping. Sequential counters are rejected: an incrementing id lets anyone walk the entire link table and read every URL every user ever shortened. A hash of the target URL is also rejected, since it leaks whether a given URL was already shortened and makes two users share one code. State the alphabet, the length and the reasoning behind that length, where uniqueness is enforced and what happens when the retry bound is exhausted.

Also decide, as ordinary decisions: what a request for an expired code returns and whether that response distinguishes expired from never existed, where the click analytics write happens relative to the redirect response, and at which layer rate limiting is enforced and what it is keyed by.

configuration is a contract, not documentation. Implementation and test authoring run at the same time from this design and never see each other's output, so anything both of them touch has to be pinned here or they will each invent a reasonable name and disagree. List every environment variable with its exact name and default. This has already gone wrong once: the service read DATABASE_PATH while the tests set LINKS_DB_PATH, both sensible, and every test that checked persistence failed.

Return one JSON object matching the schema. No prose outside it.
payload.prompt:
INTENT
Callers of the URL shortener who present a recognised API key in X-API-Key get their link-creation requests throttled against that key's own per-minute quota instead of the shared per-IP budget, while every other caller and every redirect keeps behaving exactly as it does today.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100,beta:20", LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, 100 consecutive POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from one client address all return 201, and the 101st within the same 60-second window returns 429 with body {"error":{"code":"rate_limited",...}} and writes no row to links.
- With the same configuration, 20 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: beta return 201 and the 21st returns 429; a subsequent POST carrying X-API-Key: alpha in the same window still returns 201, proving key buckets are independent.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, five POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from a single client address all return 201, proving a known key is not additionally charged against the per-IP creation bucket.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: gamma (unknown) returns 201 for the first 10 requests from one address and 429 on the 11th; no request returns 401 or 403.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS set, POST /api/links carrying no X-API-Key header behaves byte-for-byte as today: 201 up to LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX per client key, then 429 with Retry-After.
- A keyed 429 response carries a Retry-After header whose value is a decimal string of whole seconds, is >= 1 and <= 60, contains no fractional part, and is accompanied by Cache-Control: no-store.
- After the 60-second window for an exhausted key has elapsed (simulated by advancing the limiter clock, not by sleeping), the next POST /api/links with that key returns 201.
- With alpha's creation quota exhausted, GET /{code} carrying X-API-Key: alpha still returns 307 with the stored Location, and remains limited only by the existing per-IP redirect bucket (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per window).
- GET /api/links/{code}/stats carrying X-API-Key: alpha returns 200 and is never rate limited, before or after the key's creation quota is exhausted.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS unset or empty, every request, including one carrying X-API-Key: alpha, produces exactly the status codes, headers and bodies the service produces today; the entire existing test suite passes unmodified.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20", the application starts, POST /api/links with X-API-Key: delta is limited at 20 per minute, and X-API-Key values alpha, beta, gamma fall back to the per-IP limit; no exception is raised and no malformed value appears in a response body.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=" alpha : 100 , beta:20 ", X-API-Key: alpha is limited at 100 per minute (surrounding whitespace on names and quotas is trimmed).
- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, the third POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: ALPHA from one address returns 429.
- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:1", 15 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha all return 201.
- After exercising the key limiter, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today, no new table exists in the database, and the raw bytes of every file in the database directory contain neither the string "alpha" as a key value nor any client IP address.
- A 429 caused by the key limiter never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in its body or headers, and no log record emitted at LINKS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG during the request contains the key value.

CONSTRAINTS
- Python with FastAPI 0.115.6 / Starlette 0.41.3 / pydantic 2.10.4 exactly as pinned in requirements.txt; no new runtime dependency.
- Environment variable name is exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix) and the request header is exactly X-API-Key (matched case-insensitively per HTTP header rules).
- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.
- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.
- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; the existing tests in tests/ must pass unmodified.
- The existing per-IP throttle on GET /{code} (bucket 'redirect', REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER = 100) must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in behaviour; redirects are never limited by API key.
- Rate limiting continues to run as ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so a throttled creation never reaches the database.
- API key values are credentials: they must never be written to SQLite, the WAL, any file or any log record, and must never appear in a response body or header; limiter state must key on a per-boot salted hash exactly as client addresses do today.
- Limiter state stays in-process, thread-safe under the existing lock, and bounded in memory; adding key buckets must not let per-IP bucket pruning (MAX_TRACKED_KEYS) regress.
- Error responses keep the stable envelope {"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}; a key-limited rejection uses status 429 with code "rate_limited" and a Retry-After header of whole seconds.
- Configuration parsing must fail safe as app/config.py already does: an unusable SHORTENER_API_KEYS value is logged and degraded to 'no keys configured' rather than raising at import or startup.
- Keys are read once from the environment into the frozen Settings snapshot at application construction, not re-read per request.

SCENARIO
brownfield

Design the API and data model that satisfies exactly these criteria under these constraints. Every acceptance criterion must be satisfiable by an endpoint you listed, and every endpoint must trace to a criterion.

parsed.overview: A single-node FastAPI URL shortener with three existing routes (create link, redirect, stats) backed by SQLite in WAL mode. This change adds no route and no schema: it only widens the existing in-process ASGI rate-limit middleware so that a caller presenting a recognised value in X-API-Key is charged against that key's own per-minute quota instead of the shared per-IP creation bucket, with the key material reduced to a per-boot salted hash before it is ever used as a limiter map key. Unknown keys, absent keys, redirects and stats keep today's behaviour byte-for-byte.

configuration.name: LINKS_DB_PATH
configuration.purpose: Filesystem path to the SQLite database file. Tests and implementation must both use this exact name; the directory is created at startup if missing.

configuration.name: LINKS_BASE_URL
configuration.purpose: Origin used to build the absolute short_url field in POST /api/links responses. Trailing slash is stripped.

configuration.name: LINKS_CODE_LENGTH
configuration.purpose: Number of base62 characters in a generated short code. Parsed as int; values outside 4..32 are logged and degraded to 7.

configuration.name: LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS
configuration.purpose: Total number of insert attempts (initial plus retries) before a code collision is reported as 503 code_generation_failed.

configuration.name: LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH
configuration.purpose: Maximum accepted length of the url field in a creation request.

configuration.name: LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: TTL applied when a creation request omits ttl_seconds. 0 means the link never expires.

configuration.name: LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: Upper bound accepted for ttl_seconds in a creation request (one year).

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED
configuration.purpose: Master switch for the ASGI rate-limit middleware. Accepts true/false/1/0/yes/no case-insensitively. When false, neither the per-IP buckets nor the per-API-key buckets are consulted and no 429 is ever produced, regardless of SHORTENER_API_KEYS.

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX
configuration.purpose: Requests per window allowed in the per-IP 'create' bucket. The per-IP 'redirect' bucket allows this value multiplied by the module constant REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER (100). Not used for callers whose X-API-Key is recognised.

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS
configuration.purpose: Length of the fixed limiter window in seconds, shared by the per-IP buckets and the per-API-key buckets. Also the clamp ceiling for Retry-After.

configuration.name: LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS
configuration.purpose: Upper bound on entries retained in the limiter state map. Per-IP and per-API-key buckets are pruned independently against this bound so that adding key buckets cannot cause per-IP buckets to be evicted early.

configuration.name: SHORTENER_API_KEYS
configuration.purpose: Comma-separated name:quota pairs, e.g. 'alpha:100,beta:20', giving each recognised API key its own per-window creation quota. Whitespace around names and quotas is trimmed. Entries with no colon, a non-integer quota, a quota < 1, or an empty name are logged at WARNING (without the offending value's key material) and skipped. An entirely unusable or empty value degrades to 'no keys configured'. Read exactly once into the frozen Settings snapshot at application construction. Note: no LINKS_ prefix.

configuration.name: LINKS_LOG_LEVEL
configuration.purpose: Root log level for the application logger. At DEBUG the limiter logs bucket decisions using the salted hash prefix only, never the presented key value or client address.

endpoints.summary: Create a short link. This is the only endpoint whose throttling behaviour changes: a recognised X-API-Key selects a per-key bucket instead of the per-IP 'create' bucket.
endpoints.request: Headers: Content-Type: application/json (required); X-API-Key: string (optional, matched case-insensitively as a header name, compared exactly and case-sensitively as a value against the parsed SHORTENER_API_KEYS map — 'ALPHA' is not 'alpha'). An unrecognised or absent key is never an authentication failure. Body: {"url": string (required, 1..LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH chars, must parse as an absolute http or https URL with a non-empty host; other schemes rejected), "ttl_seconds": integer|null (optional, 0 or 1..LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS; 0 or null means use LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS)}. Unknown body fields are ignored.
endpoints.response: 201 body: {"code": string, "short_url": string, "url": string, "created_at": string (RFC3339 UTC), "expires_at": string|null}. Error body for every failure: {"error":{"code": string, "message": string}}. A 429 additionally carries Retry-After (decimal whole seconds, >=1 and <=LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, no fractional part) and Cache-Control: no-store, and never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in any header or in the message.

status_codes.when: Link row committed with a unique code.
Content-Type is present and is not application/json.
Body is not valid JSON, url is missing, url is longer than LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH, url is not an absolute http/https URL, or ttl_seconds is not an integer in range. error.code is "validation_error".

Rate limit exceeded before routing: either the caller presented a recognised X-API-Key and that key's bucket has already served its configured quota in the current window, or the caller presented no key (or an unrecognised key) and the per-IP 'create' bucket has already served LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX in the current window. error.code is "rate_limited". No row is written to links.
LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS inserts all failed on the UNIQUE(code) constraint. error.code is "code_generation_failed".
Unexpected database or serialisation error. error.code is "internal_error".

endpoints.summary: Resolve a short code and redirect. Unchanged: limited only by the per-IP 'redirect' bucket, never by API key.
endpoints.request: Path parameter code: string, 1..32 base62 characters. X-API-Key, if present, is ignored entirely by this route and by the limiter for this route. No body.
endpoints.response: 307 with Location: <target_url> and Cache-Control: no-store, empty body. Errors use {"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}.

status_codes.when: Code exists and is not expired. Location is the stored target_url verbatim.

Code is not in links, or is present with expires_at <= now, or contains characters outside the base62 alphabet. error.code is "not_found" in all three cases — expired and never-existed are indistinguishable.

Per-IP 'redirect' bucket exceeded (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per window). error.code is "rate_limited", with Retry-After and Cache-Control: no-store. Unchanged by this feature even when the same caller's API-key creation quota is exhausted.
Unexpected database error. error.code is "internal_error".

endpoints.summary: Return click analytics for one code. Never rate limited, by IP or by key.
endpoints.request: Path parameter code: string, 1..32 base62 characters. X-API-Key, if present, is ignored and never charged. No body.
endpoints.response: 200 body: {"code": string, "url": string, "created_at": string (RFC3339 UTC), "expires_at": string|null, "expired": boolean, "click_count": integer, "last_clicked_at": string|null}. Error body {"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}.

status_codes.when: Code exists, whether or not it has expired; expired links still report their counts.
Code is not present in links or contains non-base62 characters. error.code is "not_found".
Unexpected database error. error.code is "internal_error".

data_model.name: links
data_model.purpose: One row per short code. Schema is frozen: app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS is unchanged by this feature and PRAGMA table_info(links) must return exactly these columns.

fields.name: id
fields.constraints: PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, not null. Internal only; never exposed in any response, so it cannot be used to enumerate links.

fields.name: code
fields.constraints: NOT NULL, UNIQUE. The UNIQUE constraint is the sole enforcement point for short-code uniqueness.

fields.name: target_url
fields.constraints: NOT NULL, length <= LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH, stored verbatim as validated.

fields.name: created_at
fields.constraints: NOT NULL, RFC3339 UTC timestamp, set by the application at insert.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.constraints: NULLABLE. NULL means never expires. RFC3339 UTC.

indexes: UNIQUE index on links(code) (implicit from the UNIQUE constraint) — serves the redirect hot path, which is a single equality lookup; without it every redirect would scan links.
No index on target_url: nothing queries by URL, and indexing it would make 'has this URL been shortened' answerable from the file.

data_model.name: clicks
data_model.purpose: One row per served redirect. Schema frozen; PRAGMA table_info(clicks) must return exactly these columns. Deliberately stores no client address, user agent or API key, so the database files contain no credential or IP bytes.

fields.name: id
fields.constraints: PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, not null.

fields.name: link_id
fields.constraints: NOT NULL, REFERENCES links(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.

fields.name: clicked_at
fields.constraints: NOT NULL, RFC3339 UTC timestamp of the redirect.

indexes: Index on clicks(link_id, clicked_at) — serves the stats aggregate COUNT(*) and MAX(clicked_at) for one link; without it the stats query scans the whole clicks table as it grows.

data_model.name: LimiterState (in-process, not persisted)
data_model.purpose: Thread-safe fixed-window counters held in the middleware behind the existing lock. Never written to SQLite, the WAL, or any file. Two independent maps so that key-bucket growth cannot evict per-IP buckets.

fields.name: ip_buckets
fields.constraints: Key is f"{bucket}:{blake2b(client_host, key=BOOT_SALT, digest_size=16).hexdigest()}" where bucket is 'create' or 'redirect'. Pruned to LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS entries by oldest window_start; behaviour identical to today.

fields.name: key_buckets
fields.constraints: Key is f"apikey:{blake2b(presented_key, key=BOOT_SALT, digest_size=16).hexdigest()}". Populated only for keys present in the parsed SHORTENER_API_KEYS map. Pruned separately against its own LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS bound. Bounded above by the number of configured keys in practice.

fields.name: BOOT_SALT
fields.constraints: 32 bytes from secrets.token_bytes, generated once per process, never logged or serialised. Makes hashed limiter keys non-reversible and non-comparable across boots.

fields.name: clock
fields.constraints: Injectable monotonic time source, defaulting to time.monotonic. Tests advance it to expire a window rather than sleeping.

fields.name: api_key_quotas
fields.constraints: Frozen at application construction from SHORTENER_API_KEYS. Maps the raw key string to its integer quota >= 1. Empty mapping means the feature is inert. Lookup is exact and case-sensitive.

indexes: Dict hash lookup on the salted-hash string; O(1), no scan.

decisions.decision: How an unrecognised X-API-Key is treated
decisions.choice: Fall through silently to the per-IP 'create' bucket; never 401 or 403, never mention the header in any response.
decisions.rationale: A caller with a typo'd or stale key keeps working exactly as an anonymous caller does, and an attacker cannot use the response to test whether a guessed key is valid — every wrong guess looks like an ordinary anonymous request.
rejected: 401 on unknown key: turns the shortener into an authenticated service and breaks every existing anonymous caller.
403 on unknown key: same breakage plus a free key-validity oracle.
Charging unknown keys to a shared 'unknown' bucket: one bad client would throttle all anonymous callers.

decisions.decision: Whether a recognised key is also charged against the per-IP creation bucket
decisions.choice: No. When the key is recognised, only the per-key bucket is consulted and incremented; the per-IP 'create' bucket is neither read nor written for that request.
decisions.rationale: A partner with a 100/min quota behind one NAT address gets all 100 creations, instead of being cut off at LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX by an IP budget they were supposed to be exempted from.
rejected: min(key quota, IP budget): makes the advertised quota a lie whenever quota > LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX.
Charging both buckets: identical failure, plus per-IP counters polluted by traffic that was never limited by them.

decisions.decision: Where API keys are compared and where quotas are stored
decisions.choice: Parsed once at application construction into a frozen mapping on Settings; limiter maps are keyed by a per-boot salted blake2b hash of the presented key, never the key itself.
decisions.rationale: A memory dump, a log line at DEBUG, or a leaked database file cannot yield a working credential, and the acceptance check that no database byte contains 'alpha' holds by construction.
rejected: Re-reading os.environ per request: makes throttling depend on mutable process state mid-run and costs a syscall on the hot path.
Storing keys plaintext as dict keys: credential sitting in a heap that gets dumped into crash reports.
Persisting quotas or counters in SQLite: forbidden schema change, and would write key-derived data to disk.

decisions.decision: Parsing failures in SHORTENER_API_KEYS
decisions.choice: Split on comma, split each entry on the first colon, strip whitespace from both sides of name and quota, require a non-empty name and an integer quota >= 1; skip any entry that fails and log at WARNING with the entry index only, never its content. If nothing parses, degrade to an empty mapping.
decisions.rationale: A single fat-fingered entry in a deployment variable degrades that one key to per-IP limiting rather than refusing to boot the whole service, and the malformed text never reaches a log aggregator or a response body.
rejected: Raising at import or startup: one typo takes the service down, which is worse than one partner being IP-limited.
Logging the offending entry: prints the credential of the neighbouring well-formed entry when the delimiter is what was mistyped.

decisions.decision: What a request for an expired code returns and whether it distinguishes expired from never-existed
decisions.choice: 404 with error.code "not_found" and an identical message in both cases; expiry is evaluated in the SQL predicate so an expired row is simply not selected. Only GET /api/links/{code}/stats reveals expiry, via the "expired" boolean.
decisions.rationale: A caller cannot use the redirect endpoint to learn that some code once existed, which would otherwise let an enumerator map historically valid codes; an ordinary user just sees a dead link.
rejected: 410 Gone for expired: a precise oracle for 'this code was real', and some clients cache 410 aggressively.
404 with a distinct 'expired' error code: same oracle in the body.
Lazy delete of expired rows on read: turns a read path into a write path and loses the stats history the stats endpoint still serves.

decisions.decision: Where the click analytics write happens relative to the redirect response
decisions.choice: Synchronously inside the handler, in the same connection, committed before the 307 response is returned.
decisions.rationale: Every redirect the user actually followed is counted even if the process is killed a millisecond later, so the stats endpoint never under-reports; on WAL-mode SQLite on one node this insert is sub-millisecond and invisible next to the network round trip.
rejected: BackgroundTask after response: clicks vanish on restart or crash and stats silently drift low.
In-memory batch flushed periodically: same loss window plus unbounded memory if the flusher stalls.
Fire-and-forget thread: reintroduces lock contention on the same SQLite writer with none of the durability.

decisions.decision: At which layer rate limiting is enforced and what it is keyed by
decisions.choice: ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing. It selects a bucket from the raw scope: path matching /api/links with method POST uses bucket 'apikey:<salted hash of presented key>' if the exact, case-sensitive key is in the frozen map, otherwise 'create:<salted hash of client host>'; a redirect path uses 'redirect:<salted hash of client host>' with limit LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100; /api/links/{code}/stats is exempt and consults no bucket. Header lookup is case-insensitive per HTTP rules.

rejected: A FastAPI dependency: runs after body parsing and validation, so a 429 would still pay for parsing a 2 KB URL body, and a malformed body would return 422 instead of 429.
Reverse-proxy-only limiting: cannot see X-API-Key semantics or per-key quotas, and the service would be unprotected when run directly.
Keying on raw client IP or raw key string: writes identifying material into a structure that ends up in logs and dumps.

decisions.decision: Retry-After computation and cacheability of a 429

decisions.rationale: A client backing off gets a whole-second integer every conforming HTTP client can parse, is never told to wait 0 seconds or longer than a window, and no intermediary caches the rejection and keeps serving it after the window has reset.
rejected: Floating-point seconds: violates RFC 9110 and is silently ignored by several HTTP clients.
Omitting Retry-After: clients hot-loop against the limiter.

decisions.choice: The disabled flag short-circuits the entire middleware before any bucket selection, so a key with quota 1 imposes nothing.
decisions.rationale: One switch reliably turns throttling off in development and load tests, rather than leaving a surprise 1/min quota active.
rejected: Treating key quotas as always-on: a developer sets ENABLED=false and still gets 429s with no obvious cause.

decisions.choice: Two separate dicts, each pruned independently against LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS by oldest window_start, under the one existing lock.
decisions.rationale: A burst of traffic from configured keys can no longer evict per-IP counters, so the anti-abuse behaviour for anonymous callers is exactly what it is today.
rejected: One shared dict: key buckets and IP buckets compete for the same bound, silently weakening per-IP protection — an explicit regression the criteria forbid.
No bound on key buckets: unbounded only if unknown keys were tracked, which they are not, but a shared bound would still couple the two lifetimes.

decisions.decision: Storage engine and connection mode
decisions.choice: SQLite in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, one connection per request from a small pool, single-node deployment.
decisions.rationale: The redirect path is a single unique-index lookup returning in microseconds, and WAL lets the synchronous click insert proceed without blocking concurrent redirect reads, so counting a click never adds latency to someone else's redirect.
rejected: Postgres: an extra process to operate for a workload that fits one file, and a new runtime dependency the constraints forbid.
SQLite in rollback-journal mode: the click insert takes a write lock that blocks concurrent reads, turning the hot path spiky.
Redis for counters: a second datastore and a new dependency, for state that is already allowed to be in-process.

redirect_status_code.rationale: 307 Temporary Redirect. The service must stay in the loop on every single click: revocation only works if the client keeps asking us, so that deleting or expiring a link that turns out to be malicious takes effect on the very next click rather than whenever a browser cache happens to evict; and click analytics only exist because every hit reaches the handler that inserts into clicks. A 301 is treated as permanent by browsers, corporate proxies and CDNs and is retained effectively forever — after a link is found to be malicious it cannot be killed, because those clients never contact us again, and every one of those clicks is invisible to the stats endpoint, permanently under-reporting the busiest links. 307 is chosen over 302 because it forbids the method and body rewriting that user agents historically applied to 302: a client that arrives with something other than GET (a HEAD probe, or a POST from an integration that pasted a short link into a webhook target) reaches the destination with its method intact, so the destination behaves the same whether the caller used the short link or the long one. Every redirect also carries Cache-Control: no-store so intermediaries cannot substitute their own caching for the absent permanence.

short_code_strategy.alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz (base62, 62 symbols, no separators or padding so codes are URL-safe and double-click selectable)
short_code_strategy.generation: Each character is drawn independently with secrets.choice, i.e. the OS CSPRNG (getrandom/urandom), not random.random. There is no counter, no timestamp and no function of the target URL in the code, so observing any number of issued codes gives an attacker no information about any other code: guessing a live code means hitting one of the occupied slots in a 62^7 ≈ 3.52e12 space, which at a million stored links is roughly a 1-in-3.5-million chance per blind guess and is further slowed by the per-IP redirect bucket. Seven characters is the point where that space is comfortably beyond enumeration at the scale this service targets while the code is still short enough to read aloud and to type from a printed page; six would be 56.8 billion, thin enough that a distributed scanner is plausible, and eight buys headroom nobody needs at the cost of a longer link.
short_code_strategy.uniqueness: Enforced solely by the UNIQUE constraint on links(code) in SQLite. The insert is attempted directly; there is no SELECT-then-INSERT precheck, because that check-then-act pair is a race two concurrent creators can both pass, and it doubles the queries on the write path for a branch that essentially never fires.
short_code_strategy.collision_handling: On sqlite3.IntegrityError naming the code uniqueness violation, generate a fresh code and retry, for at most LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS total attempts (default 5). Any IntegrityError not attributable to links.code is re-raised as 500 internal_error rather than silently retried. When all attempts are exhausted the request returns 503 with {"error":{"code":"code_generation_failed","message":"Could not allocate a unique short code, please retry."}} and a Retry-After of 1; it does not loop. Exhausting five independent draws implies the table is saturated to the point where operators need to raise LINKS_CODE_LENGTH, and a clean 503 says so instead of hanging the request. A failed attempt still consumed the caller's rate-limit token, since the limiter runs before routing.

open_questions: Whether recognised keys should also get a raised redirect quota. Deferred; safe default is no — redirects stay on the per-IP 'redirect' bucket at LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 exactly as today, and the key is ignored on that route.

Whether the fixed window should become a sliding window or token bucket. Deferred; safe default is the existing fixed window, which is what the acceptance criteria measure (Nth request 201, N+1th 429, reset after the window advances).

Whether an X-RateLimit-Remaining header should be emitted. Deferred; safe default is no header at all, since anything derived from the key's quota confirms to a guesser that the presented key is recognised.

Whether the same key presented from many client addresses should be sub-partitioned by address. Deferred; safe default is one bucket per key regardless of source address, which is what 'the key's own per-minute quota' means.
Whether quotas should be expressible per window other than 60 seconds. Deferred; safe default is that key quotas use LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, the same window as the per-IP buckets.
Whether clicks rows should be pruned or rolled up over time. Deferred; safe default is unbounded retention plus the clicks(link_id, clicked_at) index, revisited if the table outgrows the node.

payload.system:
You are the API designer for an automated software delivery pipeline. Your output is the contract that implementation, tests and documentation are each generated from independently. Anything you leave vague gets decided three times, differently, and the tests will agree with the code while both disagree with the docs.

Design the smallest API that satisfies the acceptance criteria. Every endpoint you add is code, tests, docs and attack surface that someone maintains.

For each endpoint give the method, the path, the request shape with its validation rules, the response shape, and every status code it can return including the failures. An endpoint listed with only its happy path is not designed yet.

The data model states columns with types, nullability, uniqueness and the indexes the read path depends on. If a query on the hot path would scan the table, say so and add the index.

Decisions carry rationale and the alternative you rejected. "Use SQLite" is not a decision. "SQLite in WAL mode, because deployment is single node and the redirect path is a primary key lookup" is.

Two decisions are mandatory for a redirect service.

Redirect status code. Choose 302 or 307 and justify it in terms of what the service loses otherwise. A 301 is cached by browsers and intermediaries effectively forever: after a link is found to be malicious it cannot be killed because the client stops asking the service, and every one of those clicks is invisible to analytics. Pick 307 when the request method must survive the redirect, 302 otherwise. Put the choice and the reasoning in redirect_status_code, and do not leave it to the implementer.

Short code generation. Codes are drawn at random from a base62 alphabet, uniqueness is enforced by a UNIQUE constraint in the database rather than by a check before the insert, and a collision retries a small bounded number of times before returning a clean error instead of looping. Sequential counters are rejected: an incrementing id lets anyone walk the entire link table and read every URL every user ever shortened. A hash of the target URL is also rejected, since it leaks whether a given URL was already shortened and makes two users share one code. State the alphabet, the length and the reasoning behind that length, where uniqueness is enforced and what happens when the retry bound is exhausted.

Also decide, as ordinary decisions: what a request for an expired code returns and whether that response distinguishes expired from never existed, where the click analytics write happens relative to the redirect response, and at which layer rate limiting is enforced and what it is keyed by.

configuration is a contract, not documentation. Implementation and test authoring run at the same time from this design and never see each other's output, so anything both of them touch has to be pinned here or they will each invent a reasonable name and disagree. List every environment variable with its exact name and default. This has already gone wrong once: the service read DATABASE_PATH while the tests set LINKS_DB_PATH, both sensible, and every test that checked persistence failed.

Return one JSON object matching the schema. No prose outside it.
payload.prompt:
INTENT
Callers of the URL shortener who present a recognised API key in X-API-Key get their link-creation requests throttled against that key's own per-minute quota instead of the shared per-IP budget, while every other caller and every redirect keeps behaving exactly as it does today.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100,beta:20", LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, 100 consecutive POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from one client address all return 201, and the 101st within the same 60-second window returns 429 with body {"error":{"code":"rate_limited",...}} and writes no row to links.
- With the same configuration, 20 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: beta return 201 and the 21st returns 429; a subsequent POST carrying X-API-Key: alpha in the same window still returns 201, proving key buckets are independent.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, five POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from a single client address all return 201, proving a known key is not additionally charged against the per-IP creation bucket.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: gamma (unknown) returns 201 for the first 10 requests from one address and 429 on the 11th; no request returns 401 or 403.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS set, POST /api/links carrying no X-API-Key header behaves byte-for-byte as today: 201 up to LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX per client key, then 429 with Retry-After.
- A keyed 429 response carries a Retry-After header whose value is a decimal string of whole seconds, is >= 1 and <= 60, contains no fractional part, and is accompanied by Cache-Control: no-store.
- After the 60-second window for an exhausted key has elapsed (simulated by advancing the limiter clock, not by sleeping), the next POST /api/links with that key returns 201.
- With alpha's creation quota exhausted, GET /{code} carrying X-API-Key: alpha still returns 307 with the stored Location, and remains limited only by the existing per-IP redirect bucket (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per window).
- GET /api/links/{code}/stats carrying X-API-Key: alpha returns 200 and is never rate limited, before or after the key's creation quota is exhausted.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS unset or empty, every request, including one carrying X-API-Key: alpha, produces exactly the status codes, headers and bodies the service produces today; the entire existing test suite passes unmodified.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20", the application starts, POST /api/links with X-API-Key: delta is limited at 20 per minute, and X-API-Key values alpha, beta, gamma fall back to the per-IP limit; no exception is raised and no malformed value appears in a response body.
- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=" alpha : 100 , beta:20 ", X-API-Key: alpha is limited at 100 per minute (surrounding whitespace on names and quotas is trimmed).
- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:100" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, the third POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: ALPHA from one address returns 429.
- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and SHORTENER_API_KEYS="alpha:1", 15 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha all return 201.
- After exercising the key limiter, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today, no new table exists in the database, and the raw bytes of every file in the database directory contain neither the string "alpha" as a key value nor any client IP address.
- A 429 caused by the key limiter never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in its body or headers, and no log record emitted at LINKS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG during the request contains the key value.

CONSTRAINTS
- Python with FastAPI 0.115.6 / Starlette 0.41.3 / pydantic 2.10.4 exactly as pinned in requirements.txt; no new runtime dependency.
- Environment variable name is exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix) and the request header is exactly X-API-Key (matched case-insensitively per HTTP header rules).
- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.
- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.
- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; the existing tests in tests/ must pass unmodified.
- The existing per-IP throttle on GET /{code} (bucket 'redirect', REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER = 100) must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in behaviour; redirects are never limited by API key.
- Rate limiting continues to run as ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so a throttled creation never reaches the database.
- API key values are credentials: they must never be written to SQLite, the WAL, any file or any log record, and must never appear in a response body or header; limiter state must key on a per-boot salted hash exactly as client addresses do today.
- Limiter state stays in-process, thread-safe under the existing lock, and bounded in memory; adding key buckets must not let per-IP bucket pruning (MAX_TRACKED_KEYS) regress.
- Error responses keep the stable envelope {"error":{"code":...,"message":...}}; a key-limited rejection uses status 429 with code "rate_limited" and a Retry-After header of whole seconds.
- Configuration parsing must fail safe as app/config.py already does: an unusable SHORTENER_API_KEYS value is logged and degraded to 'no keys configured' rather than raising at import or startup.
- Keys are read once from the environment into the frozen Settings snapshot at application construction, not re-read per request.

SCENARIO
brownfield

Design the API and data model that satisfies exactly these criteria under these constraints. Every acceptance criterion must be satisfiable by an endpoint you listed, and every endpoint must trace to a criterion.
